"""The development ladder: the kernels Phase 1 records, and their input domains.

A *task* is a name, an input domain, and (here, for the harness's own use) a
trusted reference implementation. It is deliberately not a kernel: the kernel is
whatever a code-generating model produced and is supplied at execution time,
which is the whole point of recording executions rather than assertions.

The reference implementations live here rather than beside the kernels because
they belong to the *oracle*, not to the corpus. ``ReferenceOracle`` calls them as
``reference_fn(**kernel_inputs(case))``, so their parameter names are part of the
contract: they must match the kernel's, and they never see generator bookkeeping
tensors.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np

from autokernel_pbt.props.domain import InputDomain, TensorSpec
from autokernel_pbt.props.relations import ShiftRows

#: The ladder shapes, in the order ``Generator`` cycles through them.
#:
#: Every entry is 2-D, without exception: ``ShiftRows`` rejects anything else,
#: because a 1-D ``x`` is ambiguous (one row of n, or n rows of one?) and an
#: ``(n, 1)`` shift silently outer-broadcasts it to ``(n, n)``. Keeping the relu
#: task on the same 2-D ladder even though it declares no relations costs nothing
#: and means adding a relation to it later is a one-line change rather than a
#: reshape of the whole corpus.
#:
#: The three flavours are chosen for what they can break, not for coverage of a
#: size range:
#:   * powers of two — the sizes a vectorized or tiled kernel is written for, and
#:     the only ones where every tile is full;
#:   * odd remainders — primes and near-primes, so the last tile is partial and
#:     any masking or tail-handling bug is reachable. This is where hand-tuned
#:     kernels actually fail;
#:   * single rows and single columns — the degenerate ends. A one-column input
#:     makes softmax's output identically 1.0, which is the case where a kernel
#:     that ignores its input entirely still looks correct, and a one-row input
#:     removes any chance a row-index bug cancels out.
#:
#: MEASURED COST, which the paper must state rather than discover. Two of the nine
#: rungs are single-column — ``(1, 1)`` and ``(17, 1)`` — and softmax on a
#: one-column input is exactly 1.0 for *any* implementation. A whole class of
#: normalization bug is therefore not merely undetected on those rungs, it is
#: absent: the broken kernel is genuinely correct there, and both arms correctly
#: PASS. So roughly 22% of groups (2/9) score such a kernel as clean, and the
#: absolute detection rate this corpus reports is understated by that constant.
#:
#: They are kept anyway, and the choice is deliberate. They still catch row-index
#: and tail-handling bugs, which is what they were added for, and an asserted
#: blind spot is worth more than a hidden one — see
#: ``tests/integration/test_record_replay.py::test_unnormalized_softmax_is_caught_by_both_arms``,
#: which pins the blindness so it cannot be misread as a gap in an oracle. The
#: deflation applies to every arm equally, so the arm-vs-arm comparison the
#: project actually reports stays unbiased; only the absolute number moves.
_LADDER_SHAPES: tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...] = (
    (8, 8),
    (4, 16),
    (16, 32),
    (3, 7),
    (5, 33),
    (7, 129),
    (1, 1),
    (1, 64),
    (17, 1),
)


def relu_reference(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """max(x, 0), elementwise, in the input's own dtype.

    The zero is built as a 0-d array of ``x.dtype`` rather than a Python ``0``.
    NEP 50 promotes a Python scalar to the array's dtype, so ``np.maximum(x, 0)``
    happens to be right today for float32 — but the same expression against a
    float16 input under the older promotion rules returned float32, and a
    reference whose *dtype* depends on the numpy version is a reference that
    silently changes the shape-and-dtype comparison ``ReferenceOracle`` performs.
    """
    return np.maximum(x, np.zeros((), dtype=x.dtype))


def softmax_reference(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Row-wise softmax over the last axis, with max-subtraction.

    Max-subtraction is not a stylistic choice here, it is a correctness
    requirement of the harness. ``ShiftRows`` draws its shifts at half the
    exponent where ``exp`` overflows in the tensor's dtype, precisely so that a
    kernel *without* max-subtraction is caught; a reference without it would
    overflow on the very same rows. ``ReferenceOracle`` wraps the call in
    ``np.errstate(all="ignore")`` and would then book those rows INCONCLUSIVE
    with "the reference, not the kernel" — silently deleting from the reference
    arm exactly the rows where the metamorphic arm scores, and biasing the
    comparison the project reports.

    Accumulation is in float64 and the result is cast back to the input dtype.
    The reference is allowed a wider intermediate — it is the trusted side — and
    ``ReferenceOracle`` measures the residual against the *kernel's* dtype, so the
    rounding budget stays the one the kernel actually had.
    """
    wide = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    shifted = wide - np.max(wide, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    exp = np.exp(shifted)
    return (exp / np.sum(exp, axis=-1, keepdims=True)).astype(x.dtype)


#: Added to the row variance before the square root. 1e-5 is PyTorch's ``LayerNorm``
#: default, chosen so the reference matches the implementation a kernel author is most
#: likely to have been targeting.
LAYERNORM_EPS = 1e-5


def layernorm_reference(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Row-wise layer normalization over the last axis, without affine parameters.

    No learnable scale or shift. Those are a separate op, fused in practice, and
    including them would mean handing the declarative arm weights it plays no part in
    choosing; the normalization itself is what has interesting properties.

    Variance is the *population* variance (divide by n), matching PyTorch and every
    kernel implementation of it. The sample variance would put the reference a factor
    of sqrt(n/(n-1)) away from every correct kernel -- 8% at the ladder's (3, 7) rung,
    far above any tolerance -- so every kernel would be booked as a caught bug.

    Accumulation is in float64 and the result cast back, exactly as
    ``softmax_reference`` does: the reference is the trusted side and is allowed a
    wider intermediate, while the arms measure the residual against the dtype the
    kernel actually produced.

    ``eps`` goes *inside* the square root, which is where PyTorch puts it. Outside, a
    constant row gives 0/eps rather than 0/sqrt(eps) -- a different value, for a case
    the ladder reaches at two of its nine rungs.
    """
    wide = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    mean = np.mean(wide, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    centered = wide - mean
    variance = np.mean(centered * centered, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    return (centered / np.sqrt(variance + LAYERNORM_EPS)).astype(x.dtype)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Task:
    """One rung of the development ladder.

    Only ``task_id`` and ``domain`` are structural. ``domain.task_id`` must agree
    with ``task_id``, because the generator stamps case ids from the domain while
    every other lookup is keyed by the task — a disagreement would produce a
    recorded table whose rows cannot be joined back to the task that made them.
    """

    task_id: str
    domain: InputDomain

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.domain.task_id != self.task_id:
            msg = (
                f"task {self.task_id!r} carries a domain for {self.domain.task_id!r}; "
                f"recorded case ids would name the domain and never join back"
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)


#: Elementwise, unbounded above, and with no metamorphic partner. Its value in the
#: ladder is that it is the simplest thing a backend can get wrong: a kernel that
#: mishandles the tail of a partial tile fails here with nothing else to blame.
#: ``relations = ()`` is a claim, not an omission — no relation in ``RELATIONS``
#: constrains relu in a way softmax's do not already cover, and declaring one that
#: no property consumes would produce partner cases nobody scores.
RELU = Task(
    task_id="relu",
    domain=InputDomain(
        task_id="relu",
        tensors=(TensorSpec(name="x", dtype="float32", distribution="normal"),),
        shapes=_LADDER_SHAPES,
        relations=(),
    ),
)

#: Row-wise softmax. Carries ``shift_rows`` because shift-invariance is the one
#: law that separates a numerically stable implementation from a naive one, and
#: it is checkable with no reference implementation at all — which is the
#: tolerance-free detection the project's headline claim is about.
SOFTMAX = Task(
    task_id="softmax",
    domain=InputDomain(
        task_id="softmax",
        tensors=(TensorSpec(name="x", dtype="float32", distribution="normal"),),
        shapes=_LADDER_SHAPES,
        relations=(ShiftRows.name,),
    ),
)

#: Row-wise layer normalization. The normalization rung: it introduces mean-zero and
#: unit-variance, which are structural facts about the output that need no reference
#: implementation to check, and a division whose denominator can be driven to zero --
#: a second numerical-stability story independent of softmax's overflow one.
#:
#: ``shift_rows`` is carried because layernorm is *exactly* shift invariant in real
#: arithmetic: subtracting the row mean removes any per-row constant. Unlike softmax,
#: whose shift invariance breaks only when ``exp`` overflows and which therefore needs
#: overflow-scale shifts to be non-vacuous, this is a genuine algebraic law at any
#: scale. The relation's dtype-derived default scale is kept anyway, because a kernel
#: that computes its mean in reduced precision degrades exactly there.
#: MEASURED, and the reason this task does not share softmax's N(0, 1) inputs.
#: Under N(0, 1) a layernorm output and a *merely centered* output both have row
#: variance near 1 -- the sample variance of 8 standard normal draws ran 0.31 to 1.04
#: on the first ladder rung -- so ``rows_have_unit_variance`` barely discriminated the
#: exact defect it exists to catch. Widening the input makes an undivided row's
#: variance ~33, which the property separates from 1 decisively.
#:
#: It also fixes a false alarm. The deviation of a *correct* output's variance from 1
#: is not rounding, it is the ``eps`` inside the square root: ``var/(var + eps) - 1``
#: reproduced every observed value exactly. That term scales as ``eps/var``, so it
#: grows as the row variance shrinks -- 3.2e-5 at var=0.31, against a rounding budget
#: of 2.9e-5, which is a FAIL on a correct reference. At var~33 the same term is
#: ~3e-7, two orders below the budget. See
#: ``test_layernorm_properties_pass_the_real_reference``, which pins that margin so
#: narrowing this distribution fails loudly rather than silently reintroducing it.
LAYERNORM = Task(
    task_id="layernorm",
    domain=InputDomain(
        task_id="layernorm",
        tensors=(
            TensorSpec(
                name="x", dtype="float32", distribution="uniform", low=-10.0, high=10.0
            ),
        ),
        shapes=_LADDER_SHAPES,
        relations=(ShiftRows.name,),
    ),
)


#: Powers of two spanning log2(n) = 3..14, plus two non-power-of-two lengths so the
#: sweep is not blind to tail handling. Few rows per shape: the quantity under study
#: is the reduction length, and extra rows buy variance reduction at a linear cost in
#: hardware time.
_SWEEP_SHAPES: tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...] = (
    (4, 8),
    (4, 64),
    (4, 512),
    (4, 4096),
    (4, 16384),
    (4, 129),
    (4, 4095),
)

#: Not a new op -- softmax again, over a much wider range of reduction lengths.
#:
#: The ladder spans log2(n) from 0 to 7; the CPU measurements that chose log2(n) as
#: the reference arm's normalization swept to 16384, log2 = 14. Measuring the
#: tolerance on the ladder alone would cover half the dynamic range, concentrated at
#: the low end where the ratio is noisiest, so this task exists to make the
#: normalization question answerable on device at all.
#:
#: It reuses ``softmax_reference`` deliberately. A separate reference would make these
#: numbers incomparable with the softmax numbers already recorded on CPU, which is the
#: comparison the whole exercise rests on.
TOLERANCE_SWEEP = Task(
    task_id="tolerance_sweep",
    domain=InputDomain(
        task_id="tolerance_sweep",
        tensors=(TensorSpec(name="x", dtype="float32", distribution="normal"),),
        shapes=_SWEEP_SHAPES,
        relations=(),
    ),
)

#: ~400 KB, so the first hardware run pushed 430 KB through an A10 and used at most 17
#: of its 72 SMs -- the device was idle, and every compiled-telemetry field came back
#: constant because one fixed tile served every shape.
#:
#: These are chosen for grid depth (rows >> SM count) and for a spread of row widths,
#: so the derived tile varies from 256 to 8192 and the compiled artifact -- registers,
#: spills, shared memory, warps -- varies with it. That is the regime the device-only
#: fault classes live in, and the regime the telemetry schema was built for.
_SCALE_SHAPES: tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...] = (
    (4096, 1024),
    (8192, 512),
    (2048, 4096),
    (16384, 256),
    (1024, 8192),
)

#: Softmax again, at a size where the hardware is actually working. Not a new op and
#: not a new reference: the point is to exercise occupancy, register pressure and a
#: varying tile width, all of which are invisible at ladder scale, while keeping the
#: numbers comparable with every softmax measurement already recorded.
#: Carries ``shift_rows`` as of the corpus work, and the reason is a coverage hole
#: rather than symmetry. Without a metamorphic partner ``shift_invariance`` never
#: fires, so the declarative arm runs here with one fewer property than on the ladder
#: -- and this is the ONLY task whose rows are wide enough to reach a
#: shape-specialized defect (BLOCK exceeds 1024 only above n_cols 512, and the
#: ladder's widest row is 129). Handicapping the declarative arm on the one task that
#: can express the taxonomy's largest fault class would bias the comparison the corpus
#: exists to make.
SOFTMAX_AT_SCALE = Task(
    task_id="softmax_at_scale",
    domain=InputDomain(
        task_id="softmax_at_scale",
        tensors=(TensorSpec(name="x", dtype="float32", distribution="normal"),),
        shapes=_SCALE_SHAPES,
        relations=(ShiftRows.name,),
    ),
)


#: Name -> task. Keyed off each task's own ``task_id`` so a key and the ids
#: stamped into its recorded rows cannot disagree.
TASKS: dict[str, Task] = {
    task.task_id: task
    for task in (RELU, SOFTMAX, LAYERNORM, TOLERANCE_SWEEP, SOFTMAX_AT_SCALE)
}

REFERENCES = {

    SOFTMAX.task_id: softmax_reference,
    LAYERNORM.task_id: layernorm_reference,
    TOLERANCE_SWEEP.task_id: softmax_reference,
    SOFTMAX_AT_SCALE.task_id: softmax_reference,
}

"""The constant-input-row corner of the admitted family, and whether laws.py closes it.

Over the reals the bundle constrains a row whose INPUT is constant (z_i = 0) only through
rows_have_zero_mean: rows_have_unit_variance abstains on it by design, and shift_invariance holds
for any G o C. So the admitted family is G o C with G(z)_i anywhere on the zero-mean sphere when
z_i != 0 and anywhere on the zero-mean HYPERPLANE when z_i == 0; the reference returns 0 there.

The inherited laws.py (session 1) excluded constant input rows from rows_affine_in_input, mirroring
rows_have_unit_variance, and rows_preserve_input_order has no strictly ordered pair on such a row --
so the completed bundle of session 1 still admitted any zero-mean output on a constant row with
n >= 2. The gate's case set cannot show this: uniform(-10, 10) float32 rows are constant only at
n = 1, where zero mean alone forces y = 0, so gate.py admits the kernel below on BOTH arms. It is
demonstrated here on hand-built cases instead, with the same oracles gate.py uses.

Run: venv/bin/python scratch/constant_row_gap.py
Section 1 scores the kernel; section 2 shows the fix (judge constant rows: an affine image of a
constant row is constant) is safe for the reference and every correct variant.
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402

from autokernel_pbt.props.backends.numpy_backend import NumpyBackend  # noqa: E402
from autokernel_pbt.props.case import BASE_RELATION, Case, CaseGroup  # noqa: E402
from autokernel_pbt.props.oracle import ReferenceOracle, summary  # noqa: E402
from autokernel_pbt.props.relations import ShiftRows  # noqa: E402
from gate import declarative, load_kernel, reference  # noqa: E402

EPS = 1e-5


def _ln(w):
    c = w - w.mean(-1, keepdims=True)
    return c / np.sqrt((c * c).mean(-1, keepdims=True) + EPS)


def constant_rows_patterned(x):
    """Reference on every non-constant row; on a constant input row, the fixed zero-mean
    unit-variance pattern layernorm(0, 1, ..., n-1) instead of zeros. For n = 1 the pattern is 0."""
    w = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    y = _ln(w)
    const = np.ptp(w, axis=-1) == 0.0
    pattern = _ln(np.arange(w.shape[-1], dtype=np.float64)[None, :])
    y[const] = pattern
    return y.astype(x.dtype)


def group_with_constant_rows(shape, seed):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    x = rng.uniform(-10.0, 10.0, size=shape).astype(np.float32)
    x[1::2] = x[1::2, :1]  # every odd row constant (its own first value)
    base = Case(case_id=f"c{seed}-base", group_id=f"c{seed}", relation=BASE_RELATION,
                task_id="layernorm", dtype="float32", shape=shape, tensors={"x": x})
    partner = ShiftRows().derive(base, rng)
    return CaseGroup(group_id=base.group_id, cases=(base, partner))


def score(kernel, groups, arm):
    backend = NumpyBackend()
    failed, per_law = 0, {}
    for g in groups:
        rows = [backend.run(kernel, c) for c in g.cases]
        results = arm.evaluate(rows)
        if summary(results) is summary.__class__ and False:  # pragma: no cover
            pass
        from autokernel_pbt.props.verdict import Verdict
        if summary(results) is Verdict.FAIL:
            failed += 1
        for r in results:
            per_law.setdefault(r.property_name, {}).setdefault(str(r.verdict), 0)
            per_law[r.property_name][str(r.verdict)] += 1
    return failed, len(groups), per_law


if __name__ == "__main__":
    groups = [group_with_constant_rows(s, i) for i, s in enumerate(((4, 8), (6, 7), (3, 33), (2, 2)))]
    arms = {"bundle only": declarative(False), "bundle + laws.py": declarative(True),
            "reference arm": ReferenceOracle(reference())}
    print("1. constant_rows_patterned on hand-built groups with constant input rows (n >= 2):")
    for name, arm in arms.items():
        failed, total, per_law = score(constant_rows_patterned, groups, arm)
        print(f"   {name:18s} {'FAIL' if failed else 'PASS'} {failed}/{total}")
        for law, counts in per_law.items():
            print(f"      {law:28s} {counts}")
    print("   (gate.py cannot reach this: its uniform rows are constant only at n = 1)")
    import gate
    v = gate.check(constant_rows_patterned, include_laws=True)
    print(f"   gate.py: declarative {v['declarative'][0]}/9, reference {v['reference'][0]}/9")

    print("\n2. is judging constant rows safe? max |y - mean(y)| on constant input rows, per kernel:")
    kernels = {"reference": reference()}
    for p in sorted((HERE / "correct_variants").glob("*.py")):
        kernels[p.stem] = load_kernel(p)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    worst = {k: 0.0 for k in kernels}
    for n in (2, 3, 7, 8, 33, 64, 129):
        vals = rng.uniform(-10.0, 10.0, size=(50, 1)).astype(np.float32)
        x = np.broadcast_to(vals, (50, n)).copy()

            worst[k] = max(worst[k], float(np.max(np.abs(y - y.mean(-1, keepdims=True)))))
    for k, w in worst.items():
        print(f"   {k:22s} max |centered output| on constant rows = {w:.3g}")

"""Resolution of the affine law: how small a non-affine distortion does it still reject?

Kernel family  y = layernorm(z + alpha * z^3 / s^2),  z the centered row, s its std, so the
distortion has relative amplitude ~alpha at |z| = s and ~alpha * (|z|/s)^2 further out. Every
member is in the admitted family (zero mean, unit variance, shift invariant, finite), so the bundle
alone passes all of them; the sweep records where the affine law and the reference arm start to
reject. Run: venv/bin/python scratch/nonaffine_sweep.py
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402

from gate import check  # noqa: E402

EPS = 1e-5


def make(alpha):
    def layernorm(x):
        w = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
        z = w - w.mean(-1, keepdims=True)
        s2 = (z * z).mean(-1, keepdims=True) + EPS
        d = z + alpha * z ** 3 / s2
        c = d - d.mean(-1, keepdims=True)
        return (c / np.sqrt((c * c).mean(-1, keepdims=True) + EPS)).astype(x.dtype)

from autokernel_pbt.props.contract import load_contract, oracle_from_contract  # noqa: E402
from autokernel_pbt.props.oracle import DeclarativeOracle, summary  # noqa: E402
from autokernel_pbt.props.properties import _result, _usable  # noqa: E402

    """The affine law, then a sign check on the fitted coefficient of every non-constant row."""

    name = "rows_positive_affine_in_input"

"""Additional laws that complete the layernorm bundle. gate.py appends these to bundle.yaml.

WHY THE BUNDLE IS INCOMPLETE (see RESULT.md for the proof and the admitted kernels)

Over the reals, the four laws in bundle.yaml admit exactly the kernels  K = G o C  where C centers
every row and G is ANY function of the centered matrix z whose output row i lies on the zero-mean
sphere S_n = {y : sum(y) = 0, sum(y^2) = n} when z_i != 0 and anywhere on the zero-mean hyperplane
H_n = {y : sum(y) = 0} when z_i == 0. ZERO_MEAN and UNIT_VARIANCE put each output row ON that
sphere (UNIT_VARIANCE abstains on constant input rows, hence H_n there); SHIFT_INVARIANCE says the
kernel factors through centering; nothing says WHERE on the sphere the row lands, or which rows of
z it may look at. The reference is the one element of that family whose output row is a positive
multiple of its own centered input row, and zero on a constant row.

WHAT PINS IT DOWN

Two independent facts about the reference, neither implied by the bundle nor by the other:

* ``rows_affine_in_input`` (tolerance-bearing): within each row, y is an affine image of x --
  equivalently, the centered output is collinear with the centered input, and is zero where the
  centered input is zero. Kills every non-radial G (permutations, reflections, rotations, sorting,
  input-ignoring patterns, cross-row mixing), every monotone-but-nonlinear radial map (cubing,
  rank transforms, softsign) and any non-zero output on a constant input row. Blind to the sign.
* ``rows_preserve_input_order`` (tolerance-free, structural): x_j < x_k implies y_j <= y_k. Kills the
  sign (negation, per-row sign flips) and most non-radial G without any tolerance argument. Blind to
  monotone nonlinear distortion.

Proof that old + these two characterize the eps = 0 reference, row by row: affine gives
y = a x + b 1; ZERO_MEAN forces b = -a mean(x), so y = a (x - mean x); UNIT_VARIANCE forces
a^2 var(x) = 1 on a non-constant row; order preservation forces a >= 0, and a != 0 there, so
a = 1 / sqrt(var x). On a constant row the affine law forces y constant and ZERO_MEAN forces y = 0.
SHIFT_INVARIANCE and FINITE_OUTPUT then hold automatically (they are implied over the reals, and
stay in the bundle as floating-point stability checks). The reference's eps = 1e-5 moves the
variance off 1 by eps / (var + eps) ~ 3e-7 on the gate's inputs, two orders inside UNIT_VARIANCE's
budget, so the completed bundle accepts the reference and every kernel within that same budget.

MINIMALITY. Mathematically ONE added law suffices: "y_i is a positive affine image of x_i"
(scratch/single_law_variant.py appends exactly that law alone and rejects every admitted kernel but
wrong_shape). It is split in two here because the sign half needs no tolerance argument, and the
harness records tolerance-free detections separately (``tolerance_free`` is load-bearing metadata
in properties.py). The split costs nothing in power: the two laws together are equivalent to the
merged one over the reals.

``output_shape_matches_input`` is not part of the mathematical question (K: R^{m x n} -> R^{m x n}
has its shape by type) but is load-bearing in the gate: bundle.yaml never compares output shape to
input shape, and admitted/wrong_shape.py (an (m, 2) array of [-1, 1] rows) passes all four of its
laws. The two laws above return INCONCLUSIVE on a shape mismatch and name this law as the owner of
that finding, mirroring the harness's ``defers_nonfinite_to`` convention of counting one defect once.

TOLERANCE of ``rows_affine_in_input``: it fits lambda_i = <w_i, z_i> / <z_i, z_i> per row (w, z the
centered output and input in float64; lambda_i = 0 on a constant row) and reports
residual_ratio(w, lambda z, dtype=y.dtype, n=n), the harness's own normalized test ratio, against
DEFAULT_THRESH = 30. For any kernel that computes y_ij = fl(a_i x_ij + b_i) in some rounding
arithmetic -- i.e. every correct rewrite, whatever precision its row statistics a_i, b_i were
computed in, since rounded statistics are still an affine map -- the residual is a few ulps of |y|
per element, so the ratio is a few / log2(n). Measured on the gate's 14 judged cases
(scratch/ratio_margins.py): at most 0.10 for the reference, 0.82 for the four correct_variants/,
i.e. a 37x margin to the threshold; and within 1.3x of the reference arm's own ratio on the same
case (typically far below it). scratch/nonaffine_sweep.py shows the law and the reference arm start
rejecting a cubic distortion at the same relative amplitude (1e-5), so the completed bundle has the
reference arm's resolution on that family, not merely the bundle's.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from autokernel_pbt.props.backends.base import OUTPUT_NAME, PRIMARY_INPUT
from autokernel_pbt.props.properties import OutputsAreFinite, _result, _unusable_detail, _usable
from autokernel_pbt.props.tolerance import (
    DEFAULT_THRESH,
    ExactDtypeError,
    residual_ratio,
    within_threshold,
)
from autokernel_pbt.props.verdict import TIER_PORTABLE, Verdict

_EMPTY_DETAIL = "empty output: nothing to judge"
_NONFINITE_DETAIL = "non-finite output"
_EXACT_DTYPE_DETAIL = "exact dtype: test ratio undefined"


class OutputShapeMatchesInput:
    """Structural, tolerance-free: y has x's shape.

    Load-bearing, not an example: no law in bundle.yaml looks at the output shape, and a kernel
    returning any fixed zero-mean unit-variance rows of the wrong width passes all four of them
    (admitted/wrong_shape.py). The two laws below defer a shape mismatch here.
    """

    name = "output_shape_matches_input"
    tier = TIER_PORTABLE
    tolerance_free = True
    defers_nonfinite_to = ""

    def check(self, row):
        case_id = row.case.case_id
        if not _usable(row):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _unusable_detail(row), case_id=case_id)
        x = row.case.tensors[PRIMARY_INPUT]
        y = row.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME]
        if np.shape(x) != np.shape(y):
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, f"{np.shape(y)} != {np.shape(x)}", case_id=case_id)
        return _result(self, Verdict.PASS, case_id=case_id)


def _rows(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Both tensors as float64 (rows, n) matrices. float64 holds every float32 and every int up to
    2**53 exactly, so comparisons and centering below introduce no rounding of the data itself."""
    n = y.shape[-1]
    return (
        np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, n),
        np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, n),
    )


class RowsPreserveInputOrder:
    """Tolerance-free: within each row, x_j < x_k implies y_j <= y_k.

    The reference applies a strictly increasing affine map to each row, and every correct rewrite
    computes fl(a_i x_ij + b_i) with a_i > 0 in a rounding arithmetic that is monotone (IEEE
    round-to-nearest is), so weak order preservation holds EXACTLY for all of them: no tolerance is
    consulted. Strict order (y_j < y_k) is deliberately not required -- two float32 inputs one ulp
    apart can legitimately round to the same float32 output -- and equal inputs are not required to
    give equal outputs, so a vectorised kernel whose scalar tail rounds differently from its main
    loop is not booked as a bug; ``rows_affine_in_input`` covers that case anyway. (Known limit of
    the exactness claim: a kernel that applies two DIFFERENT rounding paths within one row, e.g. an
    FMA main loop and a non-FMA tail, can in principle invert two inputs one ulp apart by one ulp.
    The gate's uniform float32 rows essentially never contain such a pair.)

    What it catches without a tolerance argument: negation and any per-row sign flip, column
    permutations and reflections, sorting, fixed output patterns, output rows attached to the
    wrong input row. What it cannot see: any strictly increasing distortion of the centered input
    (cubing, ranks, softsign), which is ``rows_affine_in_input``'s job.

    A row with no strictly ordered pair (n = 1, or an all-equal row) constrains nothing, and a case
    with none at all is INCONCLUSIVE rather than a vacuous PASS, as the harness does for empty
    output. Integer outputs are judged: order needs no unit roundoff.
    """

    name = "rows_preserve_input_order"
    tier = TIER_PORTABLE
    tolerance_free = True
    defers_nonfinite_to = OutputsAreFinite.name
    defers_shape_mismatch_to = OutputShapeMatchesInput.name

    def check(self, row):
        case_id = row.case.case_id
        if not _usable(row):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _unusable_detail(row), case_id=case_id)
        y = row.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME]
        if y.size == 0:
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _EMPTY_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        if y.dtype.kind == "f" and not np.all(np.isfinite(y)):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _NONFINITE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        if y.dtype.kind not in "iuf":
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, f"dtype {y.dtype} has no order to judge", case_id=case_id)
        x = row.case.tensors.get(PRIMARY_INPUT)
        if x is None or np.shape(x) != np.shape(y):
            detail = f"output shape {np.shape(y)} != input shape {np.shape(x) if x is not None else None}; {self.defers_shape_mismatch_to} owns this"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id=case_id)

        X, Y = _rows(x, y)
        # Sort each row by x (stable, so ties keep a definite order), carry y along, and ask that
        # every y be >= the largest y among the STRICTLY smaller x's. With tie groups, "strictly
        # smaller" means "before the start of my tie group", so the running max is read at the
        # group start, not at the previous position. This is weak monotonicity on strictly ordered
        # pairs, exactly, in O(n log n) per row (scratch/test_laws_unit.py checks it against the
        # O(n^2) definition on random data with many ties).
        order = np.argsort(X, axis=-1, kind="stable")
        xs = np.take_along_axis(X, order, axis=-1)
        ys = np.take_along_axis(Y, order, axis=-1)
        n = xs.shape[-1]
        new_group = np.ones_like(xs, dtype=bool)
        new_group[:, 1:] = xs[:, 1:] != xs[:, :-1]
        if not new_group[:, 1:].any():
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, "no strictly ordered pair of inputs in any row", case_id=case_id)
        group_start = np.maximum.accumulate(np.where(new_group, np.arange(n), 0), axis=-1)
        running_max = np.maximum.accumulate(ys, axis=-1)
        prev_max = np.full_like(ys, -np.inf)
        has_prev = group_start > 0
        prev_max[has_prev] = np.take_along_axis(running_max, np.maximum(group_start - 1, 0), axis=-1)[has_prev]
        reversed_pairs = int(np.count_nonzero(ys < prev_max))
        if reversed_pairs:
            detail = f"{reversed_pairs} output elements sit below an output of a strictly smaller input"
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id=case_id)
        return _result(self, Verdict.PASS, f"order preserved in {X.shape[0]} rows", case_id=case_id)


class RowsAreAffineInInput:
    """Tolerance-bearing: each output row is an affine image of its own input row.

    Equivalently, the centered output w_i = y_i - mean(y_i) is collinear with the centered input
    z_i = x_i - mean(x_i). The per-row least-squares coefficient lambda_i = <w_i, z_i> / <z_i, z_i>
    is fitted and the residual w - lambda z is normalized with the harness's ``residual_ratio``
    against ``lambda z``, with ``n=`` the row width (the reduction the kernel's rounding grew over).
    The coefficient's sign is free here on purpose: the sign is ``rows_preserve_input_order``'s
    finding, and it is tolerance-free there.

    Rows whose INPUT is constant are JUDGED, not excluded: the only affine image of a constant row
    is a constant row, so lambda_i = 0 there and the residual is w_i itself, which must vanish. With
    ZERO_MEAN that forces y_i = 0, which is what the reference returns. (Session 1 excluded these
    rows the way ``rows_have_unit_variance`` does, and so admitted any zero-mean output on a
    constant row with n >= 2 -- a corner the gate's continuous inputs never reach;
    scratch/constant_row_gap.py shows the admitted kernel and that judging the rows is safe: the
    reference and every correct variant produce an exactly constant output on a constant row.)
    Only width-1 rows are INCONCLUSIVE: a single point is trivially affine in a single point.
    """

    name = "rows_affine_in_input"
    tier = TIER_PORTABLE
    tolerance_free = False
    defers_nonfinite_to = OutputsAreFinite.name
    defers_shape_mismatch_to = OutputShapeMatchesInput.name

    def check(self, row):
        case_id = row.case.case_id
        if not _usable(row):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _unusable_detail(row), case_id=case_id)
        y = row.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME]
        if y.size == 0:
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _EMPTY_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        if y.dtype.kind != "f":
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _EXACT_DTYPE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(y)):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _NONFINITE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        x = row.case.tensors.get(PRIMARY_INPUT)
        if x is None or np.shape(x) != np.shape(y):
            detail = f"output shape {np.shape(y)} != input shape {np.shape(x) if x is not None else None}; {self.defers_shape_mismatch_to} owns this"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id=case_id)

        X, Y = _rows(x, y)
        n = X.shape[-1]
        if n == 1:
            detail = "rows of width 1: any output is trivially affine in a single input value"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id=case_id)
        Z = X - X.mean(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        W = Y - Y.mean(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        zz = (Z * Z).sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        lam = np.zeros_like(zz)
        varying = zz != 0.0
        lam[varying] = (W * Z).sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)[varying] / zz[varying]
        fit = lam * Z  # identically zero on a constant input row: W must vanish there
        try:
            ratio = residual_ratio(W, fit, dtype=y.dtype, n=n)
        except ExactDtypeError:  # unreachable after the kind check above; kept for symmetry
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _EXACT_DTYPE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        if not within_threshold(ratio):
            detail = f"affine-fit test ratio {ratio:.3g} >= {DEFAULT_THRESH} (lambda in [{lam.min():.3g}, {lam.max():.3g}])"
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id=case_id)
        return _result(self, Verdict.PASS, f"ratio={ratio:.3g}", case_id=case_id)


EXTRA_CASE_PROPERTIES = (
